Corresponding Angles Theorem:

When a line (called a transversal) crosses two parallel lines, the angles that are in the same position at each intersection are called corresponding angles. These angles are always equal.

In the diagram below:

  • Parallel lines: AB and CD
  • Transversal: XY
  • The following are corresponding angles: \(O_1\) and \(O_2\)

[[jsxgraph]] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard('jxgbox', { boundingbox: [-1, 7, 8, -1], axis: false, showCopyright: false, showNavigation: false, keepAspectRatio: true }); // Define points for parallel lines var A = board.create('point', [0,5], {name:'A', size:2, fixed:true}); var B = board.create('point', [7,5], {name:'B', size:2, fixed:true}); var C = board.create('point', [0,2], {name:'C', size:2, fixed:true}); var D = board.create('point', [7,2], {name:'D', size:2, fixed:true}); // Draw parallel lines AB and CD var lineAB = board.create('line', [A, B], {straightFirst:false, straightLast:false, strokeWidth:2}); var lineCD = board.create('line', [C, D], {straightFirst:false, straightLast:false, strokeWidth:2}); // Define points for transversal var X = board.create('point', [1,0], {name:'X', size:2, fixed:true}); var Y = board.create('point', [4,6], {name:'Y', size:2, fixed:true}); // Draw transversal XY var transversal = board.create('line', [X,Y], {straightFirst:false, straightLast:false, strokeWidth:2, dash:2}); // Intersection points of transversal with parallel lines var O1 = board.create('intersection', [lineAB, transversal, 0], {name:'O₁', size:2}); var O2 = board.create('intersection', [lineCD, transversal, 0], {name:'O₂', size:2}); // Small shaded angle at O1 board.create('angle', [B, O1, Y], { radius: 0.6, name: ' ', type: 'sector', fillColor: 'lightblue', fillOpacity: 0.6, // semi-transparent strokeColor: 'blue', strokeWidth: 1 }); // Small shaded corresponding angle at O2 board.create('angle', [D, O2, O1], { radius: 0.6, name: ' ', type: 'sector', fillColor: 'lightblue', fillOpacity: 0.6, strokeColor: 'blue', strokeWidth: 1 }); [[/jsxgraph]]

Suppose \(O_1 = {@angle_corres@}°\), what will be the measure of \(O_2 \) ?
